source_snapshot.procedure: In BMC WebUI Hardware status > Inventory and LEDs, check Chassis information and detail information, then compare FRU data with ipmitool fru print.
source_snapshot.criteria: Data should be readable and correct.
source_snapshot.deepseek: YES assumes /redfish/v1/Chassis/FRU_CEMBB, disables TLS verification, passes credentials on the command line and selects only Manufacturer, ProductName and SerialNumber; it omits the required WebUI and IPMI FRU evidence.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION restores exact CEM baseboard mapping, full field reconciliation and safe read-only boundaries, but incorrectly keeps a decision gate for ordinary Project bindings.

old_problem: The prior executable suggestion could return a plausible record from a similarly named CEM member without proving it belongs to the CEM baseboard, and three Redfish fields do not satisfy the source's WebUI plus `ipmitool fru print` comparison. The prior review recognized this but treated the board map, FRU layout and expected manufacturing data as an unresolved engineering decision.
disposition_reason: Treat FRU_CEMBB as its own Project-defined baseboard identity, enumerate and bind its exact IPMI FRU device independently from FRU_ADP, FRU_CEML and other CEM records, decode the board-centric and other applicable FRU areas, and reconcile the actual WebUI, IPMI, mapped Redfish/OEM data and approved board manufacturing record. The platform-specific device/channel, layout and expected values are parameterized readiness inputs to a deterministic read-only test.
decision_basis: XLSX row 952, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, historical V3.1 record and adjacent row 953 were directly reviewed; the next pending identity was verified as Functionality row 953 / variant 77dbe7ea59c99535.
FRU_CEMBB and the adjacent FRU_CEML are separate source identities. Similar manufacturer/product data, a friendly URI or a neighboring IPMI FRU ID cannot establish baseboard identity.

The IPMI FRU format gives the Board area distinct manufacturing time, manufacturer, product, serial, part number, FRU file ID and custom fields. CEMBB therefore needs an approved baseboard layout and field applicability map, not a generic three-property comparison.

Redfish Assembly can represent assembly part, serial, manufacturer, production date and binary/original data, while vendor platforms may use OEM inventory. Standard semantics may guide parsing but cannot invent the CEMBB member relationship.

ED-02, ED-08, ED-17, ED-19, ED-21 and ED-30 preserve this board's independent identity, actual visual evidence and logs; ED-33 through ED-38 allow its finite mappings/reference values to be runtime configuration without retaining Pending.

test_case.test_name: Validate FRU_CEMBB baseboard identity, FRU layout and WebUI/IPMI/Redfish parity
test_case.purpose: Verify the selected inventory object and IPMI FRU device uniquely identify the Project-defined CEM baseboard, all applicable board/manufacturing and related FRU data are structurally readable, and every required field agrees with the authoritative CEMBB manufacturing record and actual BMC WebUI without borrowing evidence from CEML, an adapter or another board.
required_package: Immutable SUT, BMC firmware, chassis and physical CEMBB identity; protected read-only credentials, trusted TLS and serial/asset/custom-field redaction policy
Approved CEM topology distinguishing baseboard from CEML and every sibling, with durable service label/slot/association and physical-to-management mapping
Enumerated IPMI FRU device map including CEMBB device ID, interface, channel, bridge/address parameters and documented duplicate/alias behavior
CEMBB FRU layout identifying applicable common-header, Board, Chassis, Product, Internal Use and MultiRecord areas and required standard/custom fields

Authoritative Project manufacturing/BOM record with board manufacturer, product, manufacture time, part number, serial, FRU file ID, version/revision and custom values plus encoding/blank/padding rules
Service-root-discovered Redfish Chassis/Assembly or approved OEM CEMBB resource mapping, WebUI Inventory and LEDs baseboard row/detail labels and freshness tolerance
test_case.test_command: READ ONLY. Confirm the immutable chassis/CEM topology, enumerate all IPMI FRU devices using the approved protected interface/channel/bridge and retain their IDs/names before selecting the uniquely mapped CEMBB device. Execute only `ipmitool ... fru print <CEMBB-FRU-ID>` and preserve its complete output, return code and any decode/checksum diagnostics. Follow service-root and resource links to the approved Chassis/Assembly or OEM CEMBB record instead of requesting an assumed `/Chassis/FRU_CEMBB` URI. In the actual BMC WebUI, open Hardware status > Inventory and LEDs, select the baseboard—not CEML or another CEM module—and capture its complete table/detail. Decode every applicable FRU area, emphasizing Board Mfg Date, Board Mfg, Board Product, Board Serial, Board Part Number, FRU File ID and approved custom fields, then include applicable chassis/product/multi-record data. Preserve raw values, normalize only by approved encoding/padding/blank rules and compare each field to the Project CEMBB record and mapped Redfish/WebUI representation. Repeat read-only fingerprints only; never write or edit FRU, clear logs, reset, reboot or power-cycle.
test_case.expected_result: The physical Project CEM baseboard maps uniquely to one expected IPMI FRU record and one approved UI/API representation, with no collision with CEML, adapters or other boards. Its common header and every applicable area decode without reported structural/checksum error; all required baseboard and custom fields are present or use an authorized absent representation, exactly match the CEMBB manufacturing/BOM authority after recorded normalization, and reconcile to actual WebUI and mapped Redfish/OEM data. Evidence remains complete and no management or DUT state changes.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires unique CEMBB topology/device binding, complete source-required IPMI and rendered WebUI evidence, successful applicable-area decoding and field-by-field agreement with the authoritative baseboard record. A three-field Redfish projection, default/first FRU, similar value from CEML, readable output alone or unapproved normalization cannot pass. Wrong/ambiguous board identity, missing/duplicate FRU, parser/checksum error, missing required Board/custom field, unauthorized blank or unexplained source/reference mismatch is FAIL. Missing topology, layout or expected values is NOT READY; N/A requires approved platform/FRU-layout evidence.
safety_gate: Limit activity to inventory reads through certificate-verified/protected sessions. Never expose credentials in arguments or accept `curl -k` evidence.
Enumerate all FRU devices and use the approved physical/topology map; do not infer CEMBB from ID order, resource suffix, manufacturer/product similarity or the adjacent CEML case.
Allow only `fru` enumeration and `fru print` for the mapped target. Prohibit fru write/edit/upgEkey, raw storage writes, inventory refresh, log clearing, BMC reset, host reboot and power operations.
Preserve complete raw IPMI/API/UI evidence before normalization; custom fields and board identifiers require explicit layout and encoding rules and may not be silently discarded.
Use actual rendered WebUI visual capture as an independent evidence plane; API data or generated tables cannot replace it.
On duplicate mapping, unexpected sibling identity, stale data, parse error or authority disagreement, stop and preserve evidence without probing another device automatically.
expected_evidence: Immutable target and physical CEM topology showing CEMBB separately from CEML/siblings, plus the complete enumerated IPMI FRU device map and selected channel/bridge metadata
Complete timestamped `ipmitool fru print <CEMBB-FRU-ID>` output, return code, decode/checksum diagnostics and protected artifact hash
Discovered Redfish/OEM link chain and complete CEMBB inventory artifact with schema/firmware identity and certificate-validation result
Actual WebUI Inventory and LEDs CEMBB table/detail visual artifacts with the baseboard identity and required fields visible
Area-aware raw/normalized comparison matrix covering Board and every other applicable/custom field against the approved CEMBB record
Pre/post read-only fingerprints, preserved SEL/audit logs, explicit no-write/no-clear/no-reset/no-power proof and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: No mutation is intended. If the baseboard cannot be distinguished from CEML or another board, or a decode/checksum/source discrepancy occurs, stop, preserve and redact the evidence and obtain the authoritative topology/layout/reference. Do not select a neighboring FRU by trial, rewrite/reinitialize FRU storage, clear evidence, reset BMC, reboot or power-cycle, and do not automatically retry a failed DUT-side operation.

source_conflict.reason: The Master fields consistently require CEMBB inventory readability/correctness and an IPMI comparison. The partial DeepSeek command is an insufficient implementation, not an internal source contradiction.

blocked.reason: CEMBB's board-specific read-only purpose and acceptance model are determinable. The topology, device map, FRU layout and manufacturing record are bounded Project prerequisites.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: CEM topology and baseboard identity; CEMBB IPMI device/interface/channel/bridge; FRU area/custom-field layout; Redfish/OEM/UI mappings; authoritative board manufacturing values; encoding, freshness and redaction rules.
pending.execution_status: NOT STARTED; READ-ONLY FRU_CEMBB REVIEW ONLY; NO IPMI, REDFISH, WEBUI OR DUT ACTION EXECUTED

external_authorities.application: Defines Assembly identity and original-data semantics used when the vendor maps CEMBB to standard Redfish; it does not define the Project-specific CEM topology.

project_authority: The Project/vendor package is authoritative for which physical CEM board is CEMBB, its IPMI and API/UI bindings, applicable FRU layout/custom fields and expected manufacturing values. These inputs make the comparison executable without adding a human confirmation step.
